standard.title: Manipulate movement concepts
standard.description: demonstrate and explain how movement concepts related to effort, space, time, objects and people can be manipulated to improve movement outcomes
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have investigated how movement concepts (effort, space, time, objects, people) can be applied to improve movement outcomes (Y5-6). They can apply these concepts to specific situations but have not yet been asked to explain manipulations systematically.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students demonstrate and explain how movement concepts related to effort, space, time, objects and people can be manipulated to improve movement outcomes.

nodes.label: Identifying movement concepts in action
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can observe a movement situation and identify which movement concepts (effort, space, time, objects, people) are at work and how they are affecting the movement outcome.
nodes.minimum_width: Observe one movement situation and identify at least two movement concepts at work, describing what each is contributing to the outcome.
nodes.typical_width: Identify all five movement concept categories across a range of movement forms; describe how each concept is operating in specific situations and contributing to movement quality or outcome.
wider: Perform a range of movements and analyse technique based on understanding of effort in relation to take-off, body position and landing, identifying how multiple concepts interact
Create and appraise rhythmic movement sequences, identifying how flow, space and relationships to other performers are operating simultaneously
nodes.hinge_reason: Explanation and deliberate manipulation both require students to have a working conceptual map of movement concepts. Students who cannot identify which concepts are operating cannot explain how to manipulate them intentionally.

response_modes.reason: Use explicit observation frameworks that direct students to look for each concept category in sequence. Build the habit of systematic concept identification before expecting integrated explanation.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two movement concepts operating in an observed movement situation
Describes what each identified concept is contributing to the movement outcome

nodes.label: Explaining how manipulation changes outcomes
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how deliberately changing one or more movement concepts (effort, space, time, objects, people) will produce a different movement outcome, with reference to a specific movement context.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain how changing one movement concept in a given situation would change the movement outcome, with a specific reason.
nodes.typical_width: Explain how manipulating each of the five concept categories in different movement situations changes outcomes; make predictions about outcome changes before trying them; link biomechanical concepts (angle, trajectory, effort) to specific outcome changes.
wider: Demonstrate understanding of how to adjust the angle of release of an object and explain how this affects the height and distance of flight across different throwing or striking implements
Design a movement performance that deliberately manipulates space and relationships between performers to achieve a specific communicative or tactical outcome

response_modes.reason: Explanation requires causal reasoning — help students build if-then reasoning habits: 'If I change X, then Y changes because...' This structure prevents description from being mistaken for explanation.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Causal reasoning about movement concepts is transferable to biomechanics, sport science and design contexts. Students who can systematically explain concept manipulation have developed a genuinely analytical capability.
success_criteria: Explains how changing a named movement concept will alter the movement outcome
Provides a specific causal reason linking the concept change to the outcome change

nodes.label: Demonstrating deliberate manipulation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can demonstrate deliberate manipulation of movement concepts in a variety of movement forms, showing that the manipulation produces an improved or intended outcome.
nodes.minimum_width: Demonstrate manipulation of at least one movement concept in one activity, showing that the change produced the intended improvement.
nodes.typical_width: Demonstrate manipulation of movement concepts across multiple forms (game-based performance, rhythmic sequences, outdoor movement); connect biomechanical principles (effort, angle, spatial relationships) to performance design and execution.
wider: Create, perform and appraise rhythmic movement sequences that demonstrate intentional variations in flow, space and relationships — evaluating whether each manipulation achieved its intended effect
Design and refine performances demonstrating how to manipulate space and relationships between players to achieve successful movement outcomes in a tactical game context

response_modes.reason: Demonstration integrates conceptual understanding with physical execution and reflective evaluation. The full demand requires students to know what they are doing and why — instruction should keep all three layers visible simultaneously.

success_criteria: Demonstrates deliberate manipulation of at least one movement concept in a physical activity
Explains what manipulation was made and why it was expected to improve the movement outcome
Evaluates whether the demonstration achieved the intended outcome change
